newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NAB's BNZ reports 30.2 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: NAB's BNZ reports 30.2 pct profit growth.

text.p: The Bank of New Zealand on Thursday reported an operating profit, after tax and minority interests, of NZ$194 million for the half year to March 31, 1997.
This was up 30.2 percent on the result for the same period last year.
Underlying profit, excluding interest recoveries and before debt provisioning, non-debt provisioning and tax, rose 10.7 percent to NZ$209 million.
Expenses for the period fell due to the release of a large non-lending loss provision.
BNZ is wholly owned by National Australia Bank.

"As well as a strong growth in our traditional house lending business, we enjoyed tremendous growth in our life insurance, unit trust, and superannuation business, said BNZ managing director Gordon Wheaton.

He said funds inflow to unit trusts and superannuation products rose by 82 percent and 50 percent respectively over the six months ended March 31 1997, while life insurance sales increased by 46 percent.
"We've been fighting hard to develop these non-traditional areas of our business and these results spotlight the success we're having," Wheaton said.
House lending had gone well in the half year, with Auckland showing particularly strongly.
"In fact the growth of our home mortgage lending business has been as much for the half year to March this year as it was for all the last financial year," Wheaton said.
Total lending rose steadily from September 30 1996, to increase by 7.1 percent to NZ$19.6 billion. Growth in house lending was strong, reaching NZ$6.86 billion from $6.3 billion at September 30.
Income levels continued to be supported by significant recoveries from doubtful debts provided for in previous periods.
The recoveries resulted in a net credit to profit for debt provisioning of $25 million, compared with $15 million at the end of March 1996.
Total balance sheet assets were NZ$24.2 billion, up $712 million from September 30.
